artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \ge 4$, let $\phi(n,4,4)$ denote the minimum, over all sets $P$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane that satisfy the following local condition, of the number of distinct distances determined by $P$:

Local condition. The set $P$ contains no four points forming a rhombus, no four points forming a rectangle, and no four points $a,b,c,d$ such that $|ab|=|ac|=|ad|$ (i.e., no "deltoid" with one vertex equidistant from the other three).

Equivalently, every four points of $P$ determine at least four distinct pairwise distances; the only repetitions allowed among the six pairwise distances of a quadruple $\{a,b,c,d\}$ are of the form $|ab|=|cd|$ and $|ac|=|bd|$ (matching opposite-side equalities, without forcing a rhombus, rectangle, or the equidistant-vertex configuration above).

It is known that $\phi(n,4,4) = \Omega(n/\log n)$. Determine the asymptotic order of $\phi(n,4,4)$ as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: No improvement beyond the lower bound $\phi(n,4,4)=\Omega(n/\log n)$ appears in the literature. The problem is listed as an open problem in the survey on distinct distances, and a web search did not return any subsequent paper determining the asymptotic value.
